prompts.name: baseline
prompts.description: Original crossover and mutation instructions, extracted without changing the rendered text.
prompts.both: First combine the two parent instructions into a short crossover instruction. Then mutate that crossover instruction into the final instruction. Return exactly two fields: {"crossover":"combined instruction","instruction":"mutated instruction"}. Keep crossover within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens and instruction within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens. These are ceilings; prefer short edits so the entire JSON fits the output budget.
prompts.crossover_only: Combine the two parent instructions. Do not perform mutation. Return exactly one field: {"crossover":"combined instruction"}. Keep it within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens. The program will use this as the final instruction.
prompts.mutation_only: Mutate the first parent instruction only; ignore the second parent. Do not perform crossover. Be creative! Return exactly one field: {"instruction":"mutated instruction"}. Keep it within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens.

prompts.name: v2
prompts.description: Use measured parent development feedback to guide crossover and the direction and extent of mutation.
prompts.both: Compare both parents' macro-F1 and confusion matrices to identify their strengths and weaknesses. Combine complementary guidance that may preserve strengths and reduce weaknesses; resolve conflicts and redundancy using the task definitions. Do not simply concatenate instructions. First produce a crossover instruction. Then mutate it using the original parents' feedback; the crossover has not been evaluated. Choose the direction and extent of revision from the feedback: prefer small targeted edits for localized errors, or broader restructuring for widespread weaknesses. Use row totals to judge class sizes and error proportions; be cautious with small classes. Preserve effective guidance and label meanings. Do not invent new diagnostic criteria. Return exactly {"crossover":"combined instruction","instruction":"mutated instruction"}, without analysis. Keep crossover within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens and instruction within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens; prefer concise edits.
prompts.crossover_only: Compare both parents' macro-F1 and confusion matrices to identify their strengths and weaknesses. Combine complementary guidance that may preserve strengths and reduce weaknesses; resolve conflicts and redundancy using the task definitions. Do not simply concatenate instructions. Perform crossover only. Return exactly {"crossover":"combined instruction"}, without analysis. Keep it within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens.
prompts.mutation_only: Mutate only the first parent, using its own performance feedback. Do not perform crossover. Choose the direction and extent of revision from the feedback: prefer small targeted edits for localized errors, or broader restructuring for widespread weaknesses. Use row totals to judge class sizes and error proportions; be cautious with small classes. Preserve effective guidance and label meanings. Do not invent new diagnostic criteria. Return exactly {"instruction":"mutated instruction"}, without analysis. Keep it within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens.

prompts.name: v4
prompts.description: Generate two complementary children from parent instructions and task definitions in one request; select survivors independently.
prompts.both: Use the participating parent instructions and supplied task definitions to develop clear, useful classification guidance. Preserve the supplied label meanings. Produce exactly TWO children that explore meaningfully different decision instructions, not synonyms or superficial rewordings. Child A should preserve the main parental guidance while improving clarity and precision. Child B should explore an alternative organization of evidence, decision steps, or instruction structure. Make both useful candidates; do not intentionally weaken either one. Do not add new label criteria, examples, task definitions, commentary, or diversity scores. For each child, first combine complementary guidance from BOTH parents into its own crossover instruction, then mutate that crossover according to the corresponding direction A or B. Do not simply concatenate parents. Keep each crossover within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens and each instruction within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens. Prefer concise fields so the entire JSON fits the output budget. Return exactly {"children":[{"crossover":"crossover A","instruction":"final child A"},{"crossover":"crossover B","instruction":"final child B"}]}, without analysis or Markdown.
prompts.crossover_only: Use the participating parent instructions and supplied task definitions to develop clear, useful classification guidance. Preserve the supplied label meanings. Produce exactly TWO children that explore meaningfully different decision instructions, not synonyms or superficial rewordings. Child A should preserve the main parental guidance while improving clarity and precision. Child B should explore an alternative organization of evidence, decision steps, or instruction structure. Make both useful candidates; do not intentionally weaken either one. Do not add new label criteria, examples, task definitions, commentary, or diversity scores. Perform crossover only. Both children must combine guidance from BOTH parents, but emphasize different aspects of their guidance. Do not mutate after crossover or simply concatenate parents. Keep each crossover within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens and each instruction within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens. Prefer concise fields so the entire JSON fits the output budget. Return exactly {"children":[{"crossover":"child A"},{"crossover":"child B"}]}. The program uses each crossover directly as its final instruction. No analysis or Markdown.
prompts.mutation_only: Use the participating parent instructions and supplied task definitions to develop clear, useful classification guidance. Preserve the supplied label meanings. Produce exactly TWO children that explore meaningfully different decision instructions, not synonyms or superficial rewordings. Child A should preserve the main parental guidance while improving clarity and precision. Child B should explore an alternative organization of evidence, decision steps, or instruction structure. Make both useful candidates; do not intentionally weaken either one. Do not add new label criteria, examples, task definitions, commentary, or diversity scores. Mutate only the FIRST parent based on its instruction text and the supplied task definitions. Do not perform crossover or use a second parent. Create one targeted revision and one alternative decision structure as described above. Keep each crossover within {{MAX_CROSSOVER_TOKENS}} tokens and each instruction within {{MAX_INSTRUCTION_TOKENS}} tokens. Prefer concise fields so the entire JSON fits the output budget. Return exactly {"children":[{"instruction":"child A"},{"instruction":"child B"}]}, without analysis or Markdown.

Produce exactly TWO useful children with meaningfully different decision instructions, not superficial rewordings. Child A should make focused corrections while preserving useful guidance. Child B should explore an alternative organization of evidence or decision steps. Do not intentionally weaken either child.
